title: The Charge for Restoring Cover on a Keyturn Host Protection Plan Enrolment
content:
Cover that has fallen away on a Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment is put back into force on a charge the host carries, and cover then runs again from the day the restoration is recorded.

### The charge

The charge for restoring cover is the reinstatement fee the plan publishes, carried in full, with nothing added for the period the enrolment went without cover and nothing taken off for the standing of the vehicle or the host. The charge is rounded half up to two decimal places once, on the final result, and never at an intermediate step.

### The figures each plan publishes

| Plan | Reinstatement fee, USD | Reinstatement window, calendar days | Claims allowed before review | Claims allowed before suspension |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Keyturn Shield 90 Host Plan | 75 | 30 | 2 | 4 |
| Keyturn Shield 85 Host Plan | 75 | 30 | 2 | 4 |
| Keyturn Shield 80 Host Plan | 95 | 45 | 3 | 5 |
| Keyturn Shield 75 Host Plan | 125 | 60 | 3 | 5 |
| Keyturn Shield 70 Host Plan | 150 | 90 | 4 | 6 |
| Keyturn Shield 60 Host Plan | 200 | 120 | 5 | 8 |

Every figure the plan publishes, its reinstatement fee, its reinstatement window and the numbers of claims it allows before review and before suspension among them, is read from the plan the enrolment is written on.

### Worked figure (hypothetical)

An enrolment written on the Keyturn Shield 75 Host Plan whose cover fell away is put back into force at 125.00, that plan's published reinstatement fee, to the cent; on the Keyturn Shield 90 Host Plan the same restoration is charged at 75.00.
